problem: The trap contradicts the chapter and is technically wrong. Section 1 already says a constant-dwell system holds dwell time nearly fixed, yet the trap says 'Constant-energy systems hold dwell time instead'. A constant-energy system does not hold dwell time; it varies dwell time to reach a target coil energy (longer dwell at low battery voltage, shorter when time is short). A student reading both will be confused about which system fixes time and which fixes energy.
fix: Treating dwell as a fixed angle at all speeds. With points, the dwell angle is fixed, so the dwell time shrinks as speed rises and the coil may not reach full current. An electronic constant-dwell system fixes the dwell time instead, and a constant-energy system varies the dwell time so each spark reaches a target coil energy.

problem: 'At high speed it may shorten dwell to avoid overheating the coil' gives the wrong main reason. At high speed the limit is that the time between sparks becomes short, so the driver has to shorten dwell; coil heating is mainly a low-speed, long-dwell concern with a high dwell fraction.
fix: At low battery voltage it lengthens dwell; at very high speed the time between sparks becomes too short, so it must shorten dwell and accept less than the target energy.

problem: 'Corrects them for engine speed, manifold pressure, coolant temperature and knock' is loose. Speed and manifold pressure are the axes of the look-up map itself, not corrections added on top of a mapped value. Knock, coolant temperature and starting are the corrections.
fix: It stores spark advance and dwell in look-up maps indexed by engine speed and manifold pressure (or air flow), then adds corrections for coolant temperature, knock and starting.
